players.product: medium-voltage switchgear, power control rooms / electrical houses and Remsdaq automation controllers for data-center utility connection (38 kV) and behind-the-meter on-site generation power islands

quarterly_data.signal: Powell's 10-K reports order backlog of $1.4 billion at September 30, 2025, a 3% increase from $1.3 billion at September 30, 2024, driven mainly by the electric utility, commercial and other industrial and light rail traction power markets, partially offset by petrochemical; approximately $824 million is expected to be recognized as revenue during fiscal 2026. Electric utility and oil and gas (excluding petrochemical) each accounted for 33% of backlog, commercial and other industrial for 15%, and petrochemical and light rail traction power for 8% each.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $1.4 billion at September 30, 2025 (+3% vs $1.3 billion); approximately $824 million to be recognized in fiscal 2026; electric utility 33% and commercial and other industrial 15% of backlog

quarterly_data.signal: Powell's 10-K states that in fiscal 2025 the expansion and improvement project at its electrical products facility in Houston, Texas was completed and the incremental capacity placed into service; in fiscal 2024 it acquired land and buildings in Houston for approximately $5.6 million to help execute the current backlog. The 10-K also states that due to the growth in backlog, its manufacturing and fabrication capacity and its ability to recruit and retain qualified labor are challenged.
quarterly_data.figure: Houston electrical products facility expansion completed and placed into service (fiscal 2025); approximately $5.6 million of Houston land and buildings acquired (fiscal 2024)
